Hello,

I purchased a Nerdqaxe++ from HD in March of this year. Today I noticed a voltage protection error on the screen. I shut the unit off and now it will not turn back on. 

Do you have any fixes for this or do you know what the warranty policy is? Its only 7 months old and has not been overclocked or modified in any way. 

Here is the order number: Order Shop····

Respectfully, Brice P.

Hello Brice,

Thanks for the detail, that helps. I do not want to guess at that message, so first a note of honesty: I checked the NerdQAxe firmware documentation and issue tracker and I could not confirm the exact meaning of the wording you saw, so I will not tell you what it means from memory. A photo of the screen showing it, plus the firmware version the unit was running, would let me pin it down properly.

In the meantime, the most useful thing you can do is rule out the power supply, because on the NerdQaxe++ and the Bitaxe family a dead unit is more often the brick than the miner. The stock bricks are frequently marginal for what this board draws, and when one starts sagging or spiking the firmware will throw a power or voltage complaint right before the unit stops coming up. Please try a known good 5V supply rated comfortably above the stock one, with a different cable and a different wall outlet, and see whether the screen lights at all. If you have a second supply on hand already, that single test tells us most of what we need.

Two more things that would help me a lot: a short video of the power-up attempt with the new supply connected, so I can see whether anything flickers on the display or the fan twitches, and a clear photo of the serial number sticker on the unit. If at any point you notice a burning smell, a hot plug or any scorch mark on the board, stop there, leave it unplugged, and tell me, do not keep testing.

On the warranty question, that is not mine to state, so I have passed your order along and a colleague is picking it up today and will confirm the coverage with you in this thread. Nothing you have described sounds like misuse, and the fact that it ran stock is noted on the record.

If you would like a faster back and forth while we sort this, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead. Send me the power supply result and the photos when you have them and I will take it from there.

Respectfully,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Thank you. I haven't heard back as of yet but I think it may be the power supply. The blue light on the PSU is blinking dimly...

Are the PSU's under warranty or could you recommend a replacement?

Respectfully, Brice P.

Hello Brice,

A dim, blinking light on the supply is actually a useful clue. That pattern is what a switching supply does when it goes into protection and keeps retrying, often called hiccup mode. It means the supply is shutting itself down a fraction of a second after it starts, over and over. The important part is that there are two possible reasons for it, and they point in opposite directions: either the supply itself has failed, or the supply is fine and the miner is drawing far too much current, so the protection trips every time.

There is one test that separates those two, and it takes a minute. First unplug the supply from the wall, then disconnect the yellow XT30 connector at the miner, so the supply has nothing attached to it. Then plug the supply back into the wall on its own and watch the light. If the light comes on steady and stays steady with nothing connected, the supply is healthy and the fault is on the miner side. If it still blinks dim with no load attached, the supply itself has died. Always unplug from the wall before connecting or disconnecting that XT30, never under load, because disconnecting it live can damage the board.

On the matter of a replacement supply, your unit was shipped with a Mean Well LRS-350-12, which is 12 volts at 29 amps, feeding the miner through an XT30 lead. So any replacement has to be a 12 volt supply with plenty of current headroom, 15 amps or more, and the LRS-350-12 itself is the straightforward like for like choice. Please do not connect a 5 volt brick of the kind used on a Bitaxe, and do not use anything that outputs more than 12 volts, as either will damage the miner. If you want to confirm what you have, a photo of the label on your supply will tell me straight away.

On whether the supply and the unit are covered, that is not my call to make, so I have passed it to the team along with a note that you have not heard back yet, and a colleague is picking it up today and will answer you in this thread.

If you would like a quicker back and forth in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead. Send me the result of the no-load test and I will tell you where we stand.

Respectfully,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support

Hello Brice,

You are right to chase this, and I am sorry you have been waiting on the coverage answer. I have put it in front of the team again this morning with your order number and a note that this is the third time you have asked. Coverage is not a call I am able to make myself, so a colleague is picking it up today and will answer you in this thread.

What I can give you is the technical side, in case it got lost in the earlier replies. Your NerdQaxe++ shipped with a Mean Well LRS-350-12, which is 12 volts at 29 amps, connected to the miner through a yellow XT30 lead. A like for like replacement is that same LRS-350-12, and any alternative must be 12 volts with generous current headroom, 15 amps or more. Please do not use a 5 volt brick of the kind that comes with a Bitaxe, and nothing above 12 volts, as either will damage the board.

There is also one test worth doing before you spend anything, because it tells us whether the supply really is the failed part. Unplug the supply from the wall, disconnect the XT30 connector at the miner so the supply has no load on it at all, then plug the supply back into the wall and watch the light. Steady light with nothing connected means the supply is healthy and the fault sits in the miner. Still blinking dim with nothing connected means the supply itself has died. Always unplug from the wall before connecting or disconnecting that XT30, never while it is live.

Send me the result of that test and a photo of the label on your supply, and I will carry it forward with the team so the right thing gets done for you. If you want a faster technical back and forth in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead.

Respectfully,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
